editions.title: Load Factor — 16 September
editions.lede: A tour operator sells a seat on a coach that is leaving whether or not anyone buys it. Everything else in this business follows from that one fact.

editions.title: Load Factor — 3 October
editions.lede: Three British touring companies published numbers this fortnight. Each one was really a statement about a year that has not happened yet.

items.headline: Saga publishes the number most operators keep to themselves
items.gist: H1 underlying pre-tax profit £46.6m (from £23.5m), revenue +14% to £366.3m, guidance raised to £65–70m; publishes a dated booked-load table

items.headline: The rivers ran dry in July. The bill arrives in 2027
items.gist: Saga river cruises 81% booked for the year at 27 Sep v 88% a year earlier, blamed on low European river levels

items.headline: Two sets of accounts, two different kinds of good year
items.gist: Leger Shearings 2025 turnover +3.1% to £79.8m, EBITDA +21.3% to £6.1m; Great Rail Journeys accounts also filed

items.headline: Trafalgar takes three names down to one
items.gist: From 1 Sep TTC retiring Insight and Costsaver into Trafalgar: 600+ itineraries in Saver, Classic and Premium tiers for 2027

explainer.topic: The booking curve: how a departure fills month by month, and what reading it ahead of time tells an operator

companies_house.company: Leger Shearings Group Holdings; Great Rail Journeys Limited
companies_house.finding: Leger turnover +3.1%, EBITDA +21.3%; GRJ's holding company extended its accounting period to April 2026
